definitions.explanation: A delicate winged insect of the order Ephemeroptera, known for its extremely short adult lifespan of only a few hours to a few days. A classic symbol of transience and the fleeting nature of life in Japanese literature.

examples.japanese: {蜻蛉|かげろう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一日|いちにち}→一日：00942_ichinichi⟧しか⟦{生|い}きられない→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧。
examples.english: Mayflies live only for a day.
Mayflies were swarming over the river.

examples.japanese: {蜻蛉|かげろう}⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧⟦{儚|はかな}い→儚い：07898_hakanai⟧⟦{命|いのち}→命：02371_inochi⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{一日一日|いちにちいちにち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧にしたく⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When you think of life as fleeting as a mayfly's, you want to cherish each day.

notes:
The kanji {蜻蛉|かげろう} can also be read as とんぼ (dragonfly), but the reading かげろう specifically refers to the mayfly. This is an example of a kanji compound with two entirely different meanings depending on the reading.

The mayfly is a powerful literary symbol of impermanence (⟦{無常|むじょう}→無常：13422_mujou⟧) in Japanese culture. The classical work {蜻蛉日記|かげろうにっき} (The Gossamer Diary, c. 974) takes its title from the insect, likening the author's uncertain existence to a mayfly's fleeting life.

Not to be confused with the homophone ⟦{陽炎|かげろう}→陽炎：10083_kagerou⟧ (heat shimmer), which uses different kanji and has a completely different meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蜻蛉|かげろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{命|いのち}→命：02371_inochi⟧: a life as fleeting as a mayfly's
- {蜻蛉|かげろう}⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧⟦{儚|はかな}い→儚い：07898_hakanai⟧: as ephemeral as a mayfly
- {蜻蛉|かげろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{群|む}れ→群れ：00298_mure⟧: a swarm of mayflies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{陽炎|かげろう}→陽炎：10083_kagerou⟧: heat shimmer — homophone but different meaning
- {蜻蛉|とんぼ}: dragonfly — same kanji, different reading and meaning
- {蝉|せみ}: cicada — another insect symbolizing the brevity of summer
